taxonomy:
## Taxonomy (by core mechanic), using only the provided rules

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black/edge; bulbs can’t illuminate each other; each white cell illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color black cells so numbered cells count white cells to nearest black/edge; numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.
- **Kurotto**: Color cells black so each circle’s number equals the sum of continuous black cells extending orthogonally; circle cells can’t be colored.

### B) Painting / shading with geometric connectivity rules
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; orthogonally connected black cells form rectangles/squares; orthogonally connected white cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give size of the area containing the cell.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms (bold borders) with numbers = count of painted cells; white cells can’t span more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.
- **Hitori**: Duplicate numbers forbidden in any row/column after coloring; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-bordered territories have counts of additional marks; “—” and “|” have max run limits in one direction.
- **Nurikabe**: Numbers indicate sizes of white regions; white regions separated by black; black cells form a continuous wall; black can’t form 2×2 or larger.
- **Nurimeizu**: Shade cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of equal size/number; blocks are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade some cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells connected across boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **LITS**: In each bold area, place tetrominoes (4 consecutive squares); similarly shaped rotated/reflected tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares connected; no 2×2 or larger colored squares.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms (bold borders) have a number = count of continuous black cells; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; when stones “drop” straight down, bottom half must be filled with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered tiles are colored; diagonal-line cell numbers constrain count of black cells to the right/down along the diagonal’s line/column until boundary/another diagonal cell; all cells in a tile are either colored or uncolored; final picture outline must appear.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; numbered cells can’t be colored; each rectangle bordered by bold lines contains exactly one wrong number (wrong colored-cell count); colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells.

### C) Loop / path drawing (single loop constraints)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers orthogonally; no self-cross/branch/revisit; must pass all white-circle cells with area rule (straight through all or right-angled turn in all); must not pass black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through all circle cells; loop never crosses/branches/revisits; white circles require straight-through and a right-angled turn in at least one adjacent cell; black circles require a right-angled turn at the circle and straight through the next cell on both sides.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; passes through arrow cells; wind direction from black cells blocks movement against wind; loop can’t hit borders/enter black cells when bent by side wind.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop through all black circles; each black circle is midpoint of the straight segment passing through it; loop never crosses/branches/revisits.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; each bold “room” visited exactly once; once it leaves a room it can’t return; in each room loop passes all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); after moons in one room, next room entered must be suns, and vice versa.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through cell centers; must pass all “Gates” (dotted lines between black cells or to outer frame) exactly once; starts/returns to the open numbered circle; open circle number gives how many gates to go through; gate-end numbers constrain crossing order/direction.
- **Shikaku**: (Not a loop game; see section D)  
- **Slitherlink**: Single loop through dots; numbers indicate how many lines surround the cell; empty cells any; loop never crosses or branches.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop through cell centers; loop never crosses/branches/revisits; numbers show black-cell counts in arrow direction; loop does not pass through black cells or number cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Yosenabe**: (Not a loop game; it’s movement into gray areas)  
- **Nurimeizu / others**: not loop.

### D) Region partitioning / tiling / rectangle-based decomposition
- **Chained Block**: Fill blocks of consecutive black cells; each block has a size number (or “?”); every block must be part of a chain; chain can’t contain more than one block of the same size/shape (rotations/mirrors considered same).
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines; each block contains a pair of white-area and gray-area shapes matching in form (rotation/mirror allowed); block number equals half the number of cells of that color; block can contain any number of cells with the number.
- **Evolomino**: Draw squares in some white cells; orthogonally connected group = block; each block has exactly one square placed on a pre-drawn arrow; each arrow path passes through at least two blocks; subsequent blocks extend by adding one square without rotation/flip.
- **Five Cells**: Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells; no blocks with 0–4 or 6+ cells; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell (including outer frame); up to 5 numbered cells per block; lines must surround a cell and can’t enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill all empty cells with numbers; divide board into blocks; each block filled with same number horizontally or vertically; block size equals the number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges equal to island number; max two bridges between islands; bridges can’t cross islands/other bridges; bridges form a continuous link between all islands.
- **Heyawake**: (Also shading/connectivity; but uses “rooms” partitioning) Rooms are bold-bordered rectangles.
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin / Ripple Effect / Satogaeri / Sashigane / Sto-stone / Tilepaint / Usowan / Suraromu / etc.**: many use bold-bordered regions; see their own categories above.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles with the numbers in the cells; each rectangle contains only one number showing the number of cells in the rectangle.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares; uncovered white parts always form a rectangle or square; numbers indicate how many black triangles are around it orthogonally.
- **Sashigane**: Divide grid into L-shaped blocks (one block wide); all blocks must be L-shaped; open circles mark the knee; open-circle number gives block cell count; arrows point toward the knee; number of marks in a block (arrows or open circles) is 0–3.
- **Satogaeri**: Bold-bordered “countries”; move circles so each country contains exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; some circles without numbers may not move; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Ripple Effect**: Bold-bordered rooms; each room contains consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicates in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ the value.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms (bold borders) constrain continuous black cells count.
- **Suraromu**: Uses gates defined by dotted lines and black cells; loop passes gates.

### E) Number placement / arithmetic constraints on cells
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with digits from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; each cell has only one digit.
- **Sudoku**: Place numbers 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each 3×3 bold block contains all numbers 1–9.
- **Makaro**: Fill empty cells with numbers; rooms (bold borders) contain all numbers up to the number of cells starting from 1; in black arrow cells, the biggest number among up to four adjacent cells is in the cell the arrow points at; a number can’t be next to the same number in another room.
- **Kurodoko**: (Also visibility/connection) numbers count white cells to nearest black/edge.
- **Chained Block**: numbers indicate block sizes; “?” unknown.
- **Choco Banana**: numbers indicate area size.
- **Usowan**: numbers constrain colored-cell adjacency counts with exactly one wrong number per bold rectangle.
- **Yajilin**: numbers constrain black-cell counts in arrow direction.
- **Yosenabe**: numbers constrain total of entering circles’ values into gray areas.

### F) Snake / chain-like sequential structures
- **Hebi**: Place numbers in snake cells so 1→5 are sequentially connected; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; from 2→1 direction, other snake parts can’t be in the next black square or rim-adjacent squares; black squares’ numbers show nearest snake distance in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Norinori**: Place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares. (Chain-like placement in black squares.)
- **Nagareru**: (Also loop) wind-blown directed loop.
- **Yosenabe**: Move circles into gray areas with straight arrows; arrows don’t bend; circles/arrows can’t cross other circles or lines; gray area sum of entering circle numbers must match the gray area number.

### G) Graph/connection constraints (non-loop)
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally or turning; lines can’t cross/branch; lines can’t go through number cells.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (Also region/graph) bridges between islands.
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils; draw lines from pencil tip through cell centers; pencil is straight group with tip at one end; number in pencil cell gives length; line from tip goes through as many cells as the number; pencil line can’t cross itself or branch.
- **Nurikabe**: (Also painting) continuous wall of black cells.
- **Kurodoko**: (Also painting) black/white connectivity.

### H) Orthogonal run / segment constraints
- **Juosan**: “—” and “|” run-length limits in horizontal/vertical directions.
- **Ripple Effect**: distance between duplicated numbers in row/column must be ≥ value.
- **Kurotto**: continuous black-cell runs summed orthogonally from circles.
- **Akari**: illumination runs in rows/columns until black/edge.

If you want, I can also produce a second taxonomy that groups games by **input type** (bulbs/triangles/lines/shading/numbers) or by **solution object** (loop vs. graph vs. coloring vs. partition).
